question.text: Under the regulatory framework for stock exchanges, how are stock exchange bye-laws made?

answer.text: They are framed by the stock exchanges themselves, subject to SEBI approval and conformity with SCRA, SCRR, and the SEBI Act
SEBI alone drafts and notifies the bye-laws for all recognised stock exchanges
Stock exchanges have full autonomy over their bye-laws with no external oversight
Only the Central Government can frame stock exchange bye-laws

explanation.text: The Logic: Stock exchanges frame their own bye-laws, but the bye-laws require SEBI approval and must conform to SCRA, SCRR, and the SEBI Act. This places the power to draft with the exchange and the power to approve and align with SEBI. The Trap: Exchange bye-laws are not unilaterally written by SEBI, nor are they fully autonomous, nor are they framed by the Central Government. The source-accurate description is the joint draft-and-approve structure. Note: The workbook groups SEBI's power to make or amend bye-laws under SCRA coverage, not under the SEBI Act framing. The SCRA / SCRR / SEBI Act conformity check on exchange bye-laws is the rule the workbook actually states.
